title: Cas-regulation-targeting chimera enables selective and tunable control of CRISPR/Cas12a.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the single deposited file (Source Data.xlsx, 3,275,930 bytes, CC BY 4.0) from Figshare and parsed it with openpyxl: 108 sheets, one per figure panel, 6,749 non-empty rows and 158,007 non-empty cells in total. 27 sheets are fluorescence-versus-time curves (max 362 time points), 81 are small bar-chart tables (3-9 rows), and 18 sheets are completely empty (gel and microscopy panels with no numbers). The clinical panels (Fig. 6B/6C/6D/6G/6H/6I) hold 80 + 25 = 105 sample values, matching the 105 clinical samples claimed. Columns are headed only as 'Ctrl.-three replicates', '+psDNA-three replicates', 'NTC-three replicates'; there is no sequence column anywhere in the workbook.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the oligonucleotide sequences for every regulator design live in Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 (the Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out, so I never opened them), that the clinical samples are de-identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis sputum specimens, and the claim of >1000-fold sensitivity improvement. The 5ID6 Protein Data Bank entry and the molecular-dynamics binding energies (two or three numbers per sheet) also come from the text.

a1_downloadable.note: One public Figshare file, CC BY 4.0, 3.3 MB, downloaded and parsed without login or application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column. '%inhibited' appears in only 2 of 108 sheets; for any design-to-activity model the response would have to be built from raw fluorescence endpoints and joined by hand to sequences that live in a supplementary table, not in the data file.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs (phosphorothioate regulator and crRNA sequences) are absent from the workbook entirely; rows are labelled only 'psDNA21', 'pscrRNA15HPV' etc., so every sequence needs manual lookup in Supplementary Table S1.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are mostly given in headers (nM, Time (s), ag/uL, Binding energy (Kcal/mol)); fluorescence is in unlabelled arbitrary instrument units but is internally consistent.

a5_enough_rows.note: Decisive failure. The largest labelled unit is 105 clinical samples with a positive/negative call (under the 400 classification floor); the design-to-inhibition task has only tens of distinct constructs across a handful of bar-chart panels, far under 1,500.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; the whole deposit loads in seconds on a laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 105 clinical sample values counted in Fig. 6 panels match the 105 samples stated in the Figshare description; no contradiction found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Readouts are real fluorescence and quantitative PCR cycle-threshold measurements, not another model's output; only the two or three binding-energy values per sheet are simulation-derived.

existing_models.name: EasyDesign (convolutional neural network for Cas12a guide RNA design, iMeta 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Spearman's rho = 0.812, trained on 11,496 experimentally validated Cas12a detection cases (split details not checked)
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: not checked — retrieved only via search result summary, paper not opened

existing_models.name: DeepCas12a (convolutional network plus vision transformer, BMC Genomics 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Average precision 0.783, area under the curve 0.868, Spearman 0.630 on an independent test set of 1,292 held out from 16,292 Kim et al. sites

integration.join_key: none — the workbook carries no sequence, accession or standard identifier
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with no sequences in the data there is nothing to join a partner resource on.

controls.positive_control: Not applicable — project rejected before design; the data does contain an obvious internal control (no-template controls sit near 4,000 fluorescence units in every panel).
controls.external_validation: None in this deposit; published Cas12a guide-activity datasets (Kim et al. 16,292 sites) exist but share no identifier with these 108 figure panels.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is available: with roughly tens of distinct regulator designs and 105 clinical samples, any model fitted here would describe one laboratory's figure panels rather than a generalisable rule.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a short chemically modified DNA regulator's sequence and length to predict how strongly it switches off a CRISPR enzyme.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on each tested regulator design (its length, chemistry, and sequence) paired with the measured suppression of Cas12a, a DNA-cutting enzyme. I verified only tens of distinct designs exist, spread across small bar-chart panels.
plain_idea.predict: Percent inhibition of Cas12a cutting activity, read out as end-point fluorescence from a cleaved reporter probe measured in a plate reader with three replicates per condition.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building one-pot CRISPR diagnostic tests must currently tune inhibitor strength by trial and error; a predictor would save bench time. The dataset here is far too small to support one.

more_or_better_data.why: This deposit holds tens of regulator designs and 105 clinical samples; the nearest published models trained on 11,496 and 16,292 measured cases respectively.

confidence_score.why: Three replicates per condition would allow a noise estimate, but with only tens of conditions there is no basis for per-prediction confidence.

models_beatable.why: EasyDesign (2024) and DeepCas12a (2026) are recent deep-learning models on thousands of measurements; nothing here could be trained to compete.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no join key (no sequences in the files) linking this data to the existing models' training sets, so they cannot even be run as a baseline on these rows.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predicting Cas12a inhibition strength from phosphorothioate regulator design (length, chemistry, sequence context), and secondarily a positive/negative classifier for the one-pot tuberculosis assay. Both die on sample size — tens of designs and 105 clinical samples — and on the absence of any sequence column in the deposited data.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the parse: the 3.3 MB workbook opens in seconds, but building any feature table means hand-transcribing sequences from a supplementary table into 108 heterogeneous figure panels, which is where the twelve hours go.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct regulator designs with a measured inhibition value — done, it is tens, not thousands, so the project is dead in one command.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A5 decisively, plus A2 and A3. The only deposited data is a 108-sheet figure-source workbook of fluorescence curves: the largest labelled set is 105 clinical samples, the design-to-activity task has only tens of constructs, no sequence inputs appear anywhere in the files, and the inhibition label would have to be constructed from raw endpoints. A fine wet-lab chemistry paper, not an ML dataset.
